primitives.name: Task-Shard Decomposition
primitives.verbatim_quote: Datatrove does not automatically split a file into multiple parts, so to fully parallelize you should have multiple medium sized files rather than a single large file) - `shard`: a group of input data (usually a group of `file`s), which will be assigned to a specific `task`.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'N_{\\text{files}}': 'number of input files', 'N_{\\text{tasks}}': 'number of processing tasks', 'N_{\\text{shards}}': 'number of file shards', 'S': 'size of a shard in files'}
primitives.assumptions: Each task processes exactly one shard; shards are uniformly distributed across tasks.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When $ N_{\text{tasks}} > N_{\text{files}} $, some tasks perform no work.

layer2.mapping: The task-shard assignment mirrors a partition function where each task is mapped to a subset of files, enabling parallel execution without data duplication.
layer2.telemetry: Number of completed tasks vs. total tasks indicates pipeline progress.

primitives.name: Parallel Execution Control
primitives.verbatim_quote: Once a `worker` is done with a `task`, it will start processing another waiting `task` > [!TIP] > Your number of `tasks` controls how much you can parallelize and also how much time each individual processing unit will take
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'W': 'number of workers', 'T': 'total number of tasks', 'C': 'concurrent task capacity'}
primitives.assumptions: Workers operate asynchronously and independently; task scheduling is FIFO-based.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When $ T > W $, task queue accumulates and increases latency.

layer2.mapping: Execution control kernel governs concurrency via worker-task assignment, ensuring optimal throughput under resource constraints.
layer2.telemetry: Worker utilization ratio and queue depth monitor system efficiency.

primitives.name: Resilient Task Tracking
primitives.verbatim_quote: Datatrove keeps track of which tasks have completed and when you relaunch only incomplete tasks will run.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'M_{\\text{complete}}': 'marker file indicating task completion', 'L_{\\text{dir}}': 'logging directory path', 'F_{\\text{failures}}': 'set of failed task identifiers'}
primitives.assumptions: Task completion is tracked via atomic file creation; failure recovery is deterministic.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Upon relaunch, only tasks without $ M_{\text{complete}} $ in $ L_{\text{dir}}/completions $ are re-executed.

layer2.mapping: Completion tracking mirrors a state-machine protocol where each task's terminal state is recorded in a persistent log.
layer2.telemetry: Percentage of resumed tasks versus newly launched tasks reflects robustness against interruptions.
